subject: Request: Narrow 'Generated Content' Indemnity — defense control sequencing & evidence custodian SLA
messages:
From: Elliot Zhang <elliot@pixelpath.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: PixelPath Legal <legal@pixelpath.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form negotiation — indemnity for generated content

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the call earlier. Our legal team asked me to follow up with a specific ask: PixelPath needs the Order Form indemnity to explicitly cover third-party claims alleging that generated content ("Assistant Output") infringes a third party's IP, unless the output is solely derivative of customer-provided content.

We understand Redwood's standard approach is to limit customer indemnity in certain AI-output scenarios, but PixelPath is asking for: 1) a defend-and-indemnify commitment for third-party infringement claims related to generated content; 2) the ability to take control of defense if Redwood does not step in within a 14-day cure window; and 3) a documented evidence custodian SLA so we can collect required artifacts for litigation (logs, prompt/response bundles, and model metadata) for at least 180 days.

I attached our proposed redlines (pixelpath_indemnity_redlines.pdf). Can your team confirm whether the defense-control sequencing (14-day window) and the 180-day evidence retention are acceptable, or propose alternatives?

Appreciate a concise point of contact on this — we prefer to keep the procurement thread tight.

Best,
Elliot
Product Counsel, PixelPath

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Zhang <elliot@pixelpath.ai>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form negotiation — indemnity for generated content

Elliot — thanks for sending the redlines and for the clear summary. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Karthik (sales/ops) to coordinate. A few quick clarifications from our side before we dig into the contract language: 

- "Generated content" can be broad — can you confirm whether PixelPath is referring to outputs from models Redwood serves on behalf of the customer (hosted/dedicated/private) or also to customer-supplied fine-tuned/exported models?
- Is PixelPath willing to accept a limited carveout for claims solely caused by customer prompt engineering that intentionally induces infringing output?
- For evidence retention, is 180 days a hard requirement or a negotiable target (we typically retain detailed prompt+response bundles for 90 days in hosted by default; dedicated/private retention can be configured but may need an add-on).

On sequencing: Redwood's standard defend-control process is: Redwood offers defense within 30 days of notice; if Redwood declines or doesn't respond, the customer may conduct defense with Redwood's consent (reasonable). We can discuss shortening to 14 days with a narrowing of scope or additional insurance/limits.

Next steps: Kimberly, can you review the attached redlines and flag language we should push back on (defense-control timing, retention period, cap interaction)? Karthik — should we propose a compensating commercial concession (term credit or escrow) if we concede on defense-control timing?

I'll consolidate and get back to Elliot with a proposed compromise by Friday.

Thanks — Mina
Sr. Contracts Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: 1) references PixelPath redlines

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Order Form negotiation — indemnity for generated content

Mina / team — quick read of Elliot's redlines attached. Key positions I recommend we hold or compromise around: 

1) Defense-control timing: push to 21 days instead of 14. We can agree to 21 days + an express commitment to escalate to Redwood execs on non-response. A 14-day automatic transfer worries us operationally (we may need access to counsel and case info).

2) Evidence retention SLA: counter-propose 120 days for hosted as standard, with an explicit optional add-on for 180/365 days at additional cost for Dedicated/Private customers. Include an "export bundle" spec and a request process (authenticated API + security review) rather than open access.

3) Scope carveouts: accept a responsibility carveout for outputs that are verbatim reproductions of customer-supplied copyrighted content; reject blanket exclusions tied to "prompt engineering" without specificity. Suggest: exclude claims where customer provided the infringing content or instructed the model to reproduce it.

4) Cap / insurance: if we accept the shorter defense window, require either (a) a modest uplift in the per-month fee or (b) a limited indemnity cap tied to the order form value (e.g., 1x annual recurring spend) and requirement that customer maintain minimum commercial liability insurance.

I'll draft proposed language this afternoon. Karthik — can you get pricing delta scenarios for a 21-day vs 14-day defense window and a 120 vs 180 day retention add-on?

K
Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference

Attachment: 1) internal redline notes (summary)

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: Elliot Zhang <elliot@pixelpath.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2026 16:43:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Order Form negotiation — indemnity for generated content

Elliot / team — thanks for patience. Based on legal input (below) and ops constraints, here's a commercial proposal we can take to PixelPath: 

- Defense-control sequencing: Redwood will commit to providing a written position on defense within 21 days of notice. If Redwood does not engage in good faith within 21 days, PixelPath may assume defense control provided Redwood is given a 7-day "reconsideration" window during which we will produce a good-faith statement and cooperating counsel. Total potential delta = 28 days, but automatic transfer only after 28 days (21 + 7).

- Evidence retention SLA: Standard retention (hosted) = 90 days for raw prompt/response bundles; we will provide an "export bundle" (logs + model metadata + hashes) on request for 120 days. PixelPath may purchase a 180-day retention add-on for dedicated/private deployments at a one-time configuration fee + $0.03/GB/month for storage.

- Scope: Redwood accepts an explicit carveout excluding claims that arise solely from customer-supplied copyrighted material or instructions to verbatim reproduce content. We will not accept indemnity for scenarios where the customer intentionally instructs the model to infringe.

- Cap/insurance: If PixelPath insists on the shorter transfer timing (automatic at 14 days), we will require a limited increase to the order value (one-time setup credit reduction of 10%) or minimum $5M commercial liability insurance endorsement naming Redwood as an additional insured for related claims.

Action items: 
- Elliot, please confirm whether PixelPath can accept the 21+7 sequencing (auto-transfer at 28 days) and the 120-day export bundle baseline. If not, let us know which items are deal-breakers so we can escalate.
- Kimberly, Mina — I'll coordinate a short SOW addendum for the retention add-on pricing and update the order form pricing sheet.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence_retention_matrix.xlsx (pricing and storage math)
